findings.summary: The Ohm's-law worked example rendered the current variable as the Turkish word ben.
evidence: The source formula uses the protected current variable I, while the target string contained ben.
findings.resolution: Restored the canonical I variable and preserved the localized numeric formatting.

findings.summary: The milliampere conversion omitted spaces around the unit symbol.
evidence: The previous target text was 1mA = 0,001A, unlike the surrounding SI expressions.

findings.summary: The Joule-heating example localized the SI second symbol as sn.
evidence: The formula displayed 10 sn, while the canonical SI symbol is s.
findings.resolution: Restored the SI expression E = P × t = 7,2 W × 10 s = 72 J.

findings.summary: The Joule-heating conclusion used an awkward rate expression.
evidence: The previous wording combined the time rate and total energy in a literal phrase.
findings.resolution: Rephrased the sentence as a natural statement of 7,2 joules per second and 72 J in 10 seconds.

findings.summary: The right-triangle formulas still exposed English side names in Turkish content.
evidence: The displayed formulas used opposite, adjacent, and hypotenuse despite the surrounding Turkish explanation.
findings.resolution: Localized the visible opposite-side name to karşı while preserving the trigonometric expression.

findings.summary: The cosine formula still exposed the English adjacent-side name.
evidence: The displayed formula used adjacent in otherwise Turkish explanatory content.
findings.resolution: Localized the visible adjacent-side name to komşu.

findings.summary: The tangent formula still exposed English side names.
evidence: The displayed formula used opposite and adjacent rather than the established Turkish terms.
findings.resolution: Localized the visible side names to karşı and komşu.
